sentences.en: And so the, the month we started was the, I want to say it was like July or somewhere in there, 2005.

sentences.en: And that was when, uh, Apple first started supporting podcasts.
sentences.zh: 那就是苹果首次开始支持播客的时候。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like turning up in the Klondike before anyone's arrived.
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉就像是在淘金热到来之前就赶到了克朗代克。

sentences.en: The bottom line is, it's just absolute serendipitous luck.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这完全是妙不可言的运气。

sentences.en: And it's taught me, I think a lot about history where you look and you go, okay, so a lot of things maybe fall into that same category
sentences.zh: 我觉得这让我对历史有了很多思考，你会发现，很多事情或许都属于这一类，

sentences.en: where you say, how did Julius Caesar end up in this place at this time?
sentences.zh: 你会问，为什么尤利乌斯·恺撒会在那个时间出现在那个地方？

sentences.en: Was it Julius Caesar's doing, or was he just lucky?
sentences.zh: 那是尤利乌斯·恺撒刻意为之，还是他只是走运？

sentences.en: And on the topics.
sentences.zh: 说到这些主题。

sentences.en: So for those people, your, your podcast is called hardcore history.
sentences.zh: 对于那些人来说，你的，你的播客叫硬核历史。

sentences.en: And I mean, it is pretty hardcore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它确实挺硬核的。

sentences.en: It really makes us look positively soft core, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这真让我们显得相形见绌，变得好软核。

sentences.en: That's not something I'd often say about us, um, by comparison, because your episodes are enormous.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，我通常不会这样评价我们自己，因为你的节目体量太巨大了。

sentences.en: You'll do a sort of series on the Pacific war and it's sort of five episodes that are five hours each.
sentences.zh: 你会做一个关于太平洋战争的系列，大概有五集，每集五个小时。

sentences.en: So have you memorized all the stuff beforehand or how does that work?
sentences.zh: 所以你事先把所有内容都背下来了吗？这是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Well, let me just say that the first episode we ever did was 16 minutes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我先说，我们做过的第一期节目只有16分钟。

sentences.en: So that shows you what I was thinking it was going to be.
sentences.zh: 所以这说明了我当时对它的设想。

sentences.en: So this evolution is totally contrary to anything I would have chosen because as you guys know, as podcasters yourself, it is really hard to do five and a half
sentences.zh: 所以这种演变完全违背了我的初衷，因为正如你们这些播客同行所知，要做五個半

sentences.en: hour long shows and then listen to them and edit them and all that.
sentences.zh: 小时的节目，然后还要去听、去剪辑，以及做所有这些工作，真的很艰难。

sentences.en: And then all the stuff that ends up on the cutting room floor.
sentences.zh: 还有那些最终被剪掉的废弃片段。

sentences.en: Um, I, I, I, in terms of memorization, no, I have to do all of the prep ahead of time in terms of a lot of these topics are things I knew something about anyway, right?
sentences.zh: 至于背诵，完全没有，我必须提前做好所有准备工作，因为很多主题本身就是我原本就略知一二的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not starting from ground zero.
sentences.zh: 我并不是从零开始。

sentences.en: I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我不是的。

sentences.en: Somebody said to me once, why would you please do a show on 17th century India?
sentences.zh: 曾经有人对我说，你为什么不做一期关于17世纪印度的节目？

sentences.en: And I said, I can't do a show on 17th century.
sentences.zh: 我说，我不能做一期关于17世纪的节目。

sentences.en: I know nothing about 17th century India and I need to know something.
sentences.zh: 我对17世纪的印度一无所知，我需要去了解一些情况。

sentences.en: But so the process when you decide on the topic is okay, how much of that information I used to know is still valid, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以当你决定好主题后，这个过程就是：好吧，我以前掌握的那些信息现在还有多少是有效的？

sentences.en: And so you start from the foundational level there and you read a lot.
sentences.zh: 于是你就从基础层面开始，大量阅读。

sentences.en: And then I usually mark down little quotes that I want to include in the program, but then we go in and we sort of freewheel because it
sentences.zh: 然后我通常会记下一些想包含在节目里的小语录，但接着我们就会即兴发挥，因为

sentences.en: ends up becoming something that you never could have planned for better or for worse, if that makes sense from an evolutionary standpoint.
sentences.zh: 从进化的角度来看，如果这说得通的话，它最终会变成一种你无论如何也计划不出来的东西，无论是好是坏。

sentences.en: And Dan, what, what you also do, so you, you great narrative sweep, but you also, you focus in on, on the big questions that I'm sure people are always asking themselves.
sentences.zh: 丹，你所做的事情还有，你拥有宏大的叙事视野，但你同时也专注于那些人们肯定经常自问的重大问题。

sentences.en: So Alexander or Hitler, are they really so different?
sentences.zh: 所以，亚历山大还是希特勒，他们真的有那么大区别吗？

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: And so that was really our inspiration for what we thought we, we talk about with you.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实成为了我们的灵感来源，让我们思考可以和你讨论什么。

sentences.en: As Dominic said, we, we have discussed some of the big, big questions of history on our podcast, but we thought that to go to the next league.
sentences.zh: 正如多米尼克所说，我们在播客中探讨过一些历史上的重大问题，但我们觉得要想迈上新台阶。

sentences.en: We've got you here.
sentences.zh: 我们把你请到了这里。

sentences.en: We could ask you perhaps 10 questions that we've prepared in advance and we could discuss them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以向你提出我们提前准备好的大约10个问题，并进行讨论。

sentences.en: And I think that these are the 10 that we've chosen are absolutely probably the 10 biggest questions in the whole field of history.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们挑选的这10个问题，绝对可以说是整个历史领域中最重要的10个问题。

sentences.en: That's a very big claim, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这个口气很大啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: I should say for our listeners, our regular listeners, we obviously didn't prepare them together because there would be far too much bickering.
sentences.zh: 我得对我们的听众，我们的老听众说，这些显然不是我们一起准备的，因为那样争吵会太多了。

sentences.en: So we each prepared five, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 所以我们各自准备了五个，对吧？

sentences.en: You can judge who chose serious, intelligent, wide ranging questions and who chose the sort of questions that you'd see on a quiz machine at a pub in 1988.
sentences.zh: 你可以评判一下，谁挑选了严肃、睿智、涉猎广泛的问题，而谁挑选的则是那种你在1988年酒吧机智问答机上才会看到的问题。

sentences.en: I want you guys to know something.
sentences.zh: 我想让你们知道一件事。

sentences.en: When we decided to do the history show, my original intention was to do it for people like you, right?
sentences.zh: 当我们决定做这个历史节目时，我最初的意图是为你们这样的人做的，对吧？

sentences.en: I had never intended to do shows for people that didn't know the history.
sentences.zh: 我从来没想过为那些不懂历史的人做节目。

sentences.en: Tom, what does he mean by people like us?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他说的“像我们这样的人”是什么意思？

sentences.en: I mean, people that know the history, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，懂历史的人，对吧？

sentences.en: And so we were just going to talk about the weird questions that you were referring to.
sentences.zh: 所以我们本来只打算讨论你刚才提到的那些稀奇古怪的问题。

sentences.en: And I thought, okay, I'm not qualified to teach anybody history, but I can talk about the weird questions.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我没有资格教任何人历史，但我可以讨论那些古怪的问题。

sentences.en: And it was only when you found out that a lot of the listeners didn't know the background story that we started giving more background.
sentences.zh: 直到你发现很多听众并不了解背景故事，我们才开始提供更多的背景。

sentences.en: But my intention had been to talk to people like you who knew this stuff and then just say, isn't it weird that, you know, blank, blank, blank.
sentences.zh: 但我的本意是和你们这样懂这些内容的人对话，然后直接说：“不是很奇怪吗，你知道的，空白，空白，空白。”

sentences.en: So go ahead, the questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，请出题吧。

sentences.en: Yes, we'll see what we can maul.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们来看看能把哪个问题搞砸。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 那么，这是第一个问题。

sentences.en: I think this is probably the biggest question of all.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能是所有问题中最大的一个。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that religious professors at Oxford and Cambridge would agree with me on this.
sentences.zh: 我确信牛津和剑桥的宗教教授们也会对此表示赞同。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 那么我们开始了。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Dan, who would you least like to be besieged by?
sentences.zh: 丹，你最不愿意被谁围城？

sentences.en: A, the Assyrians,
sentences.zh: A，亚述人，

sentences.en: B, the Romans, or C, the Mongols?
sentences.zh: B，罗马人，还是 C，蒙古人？

sentences.en: I'll repeat.
sentences.zh: 我再重复一遍。

sentences.en: Do you need to repeat?
sentences.zh: 你需要重复吗？

sentences.en: A, the Assyrians,
sentences.zh: A，亚述人，

sentences.en: B, the Romans, or C, the Mongols?
sentences.zh: B，罗马人，还是 C，蒙古人？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 所以我有一个澄清性质的小问题。

sentences.en: Who am I?
sentences.zh: 我是谁？

sentences.en: Am I just a common citizen in this city or am I someone in a leadership or position of authority?
sentences.zh: 我是城里的一名普通公民，还是担任领导或权力职位的人？

sentences.en: I think that's up to you.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这由你决定。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a fruitful avenue to discuss.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个值得探讨的有意义的方向。

sentences.en: So let's start off by saying that you are the person in charge of the city.
sentences.zh: 那我们首先假设你是这座城市的负责人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Then I'm going to say I want to be besieged by the Mongols because I think they have the least good chance of getting into the city.
sentences.zh: 那我要说，我希望被蒙古人围城，因为我认为他们攻入这座城市的几率是最低的。

sentences.en: I think the Assyrians and the Romans, it's going to be a hundred percent.
sentences.zh: 我认为亚述人和罗马人，那将是百分之百。

sentences.en: I'm in deep trouble.
sentences.zh: 我可就大难临头了。

sentences.en: Whereas the Mongols sometimes didn't have the greatest siege situation.
sentences.zh: 而蒙古人有时并没有最出色的攻城战术。

sentences.en: It depends on who they captured and who they were bringing with them.
sentences.zh: 这取决于他们俘虏了谁，以及他们带了什么人随行。

sentences.en: But I mean, if you catch the Mongols at certain periods of time and in certain venues, sometimes they had a harder time.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，如果你在某些时期、某些地点遇到蒙古人，有时他们也会遇到困难。

sentences.en: The Romans and the Assyrians always had their gear with them.
sentences.zh: 罗马人和亚述人总是随身携带装备。

sentences.en: They were ready for sieges most of the time.
sentences.zh: 他们大部分时间都为攻城做好了准备。

sentences.en: The Mongols, sometimes it would have been just as devastating.
sentences.zh: 对蒙古人来说，有时他们造成的毁灭性会同样巨大。

sentences.en: Other times they might have ridden around your walls for a long time and not been able to do much.
sentences.zh: 而另一些时候，他们可能会在你的城墙外转悠很长时间，却束手无策。

sentences.en: So if I'm the leadership, in which case I'm dying with any of these people get a hold of me, then I think the
sentences.zh: 所以如果我是领导层，这种情况下无论这些人中的哪一个抓住我，我都死定了，那我认为

sentences.en: Mongols have, and they all probably have a pretty good chance of taking my city, but I think they have the least good chance of those three individual groups.

sentences.en: Maybe that's a good way for it.
sentences.zh: 也许这样说挺合适的。

sentences.en: I think that's it.
sentences.zh: 我想就是这样。

sentences.en: I'd answer the Mongols, Tom, but for a different reason.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我会选蒙古人，但原因不同。

sentences.en: Am I not right in thinking that if, I mean, I know, Dan, you've done a podcast about Genghis Khan, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，丹，你好像做过一期关于成吉思汗的播客，对吧？

sentences.en: And we did one about, a couple about Genghis Khan a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我们几周前也做过关于成吉思汗的几期节目。

sentences.en: Am I not right in thinking that the Mongols, if you surrender immediately, you can probably collaborate with them?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，如果蒙古人来袭，如果你立刻投降，你或许可以和他们合作，对吗？

sentences.en: So you're saying you take the coward's option, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 所以你是说你选择当懦夫，多米尼克？

sentences.en: I don't think it's a coward's option, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是懦夫的选择，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think it's that, given that the alternative is to be part of a pyramid of skulls.
sentences.zh: 我认为，考虑到另一种选择是成为人头骷髅塔的一部分。

sentences.en: As I have already said, you have the heart of a eunuch.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，你有一颗太监的心。

sentences.en: We call that living to fight another day, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我们管这叫留得青山在，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's the alternative brave option.
sentences.zh: 这是勇敢的备选方案。

sentences.en: So Tom, what do you think the answer should have been?
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆，你觉得答案应该是什么？
